newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end firmer, seen stable to expiry.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end firmer, seen stable to expiry.

text.p: Austria's ATX index ended on a robust note on Wednesday helped by weaker-than-expected U.S. inflation data and strong demand in individual shares, traders said and predicted a stable run to the end of the week.
The ATX index rose 5.30 points or 0.42 percent to 1,261.47. Among its constituents 14 shares gained, seven fell.
Traders said they had expected moderate downside but that strong demand in Creditanstalt preferred shares, beverage group BBAG and brewer unit Brau Union had influenced the pick-up.
"We recovered well in the course of the day," said one trader.
Traders said U.S. producer prices indicating a lower chance of a U.S. rate hike contributed to the rise.
"That dampens interest fears. That is good for the market," said one trader.
The expiry of futures and options on Friday is no longer seen as a major factor since most investors have already taken up their positions, traders said.
The ATX was expected to come under pressure on Thursday when Vienna airport operator Flughafen goes ex-dividend.
The top gainer was Creditanstalt preferred, up 4.54 at 505.60 schillings.
Fireproof material maker Radex Heraklith RHIV was the biggest decliner, down 0.94 at 525 schillings.
The May ATX contract added 19.10 points at 1,259.0.
